enquiry: We handle a petroleum stream and currently send samples to a laboratory for water determination. We want to investigate a fiber based measurement closer to the process so that changes can be noticed sooner. The analyzer would be outside the process area. Before selecting equipment, we need to know what to clarify and what a first comparison experiment should establish.

intake.summary: The customer wants to know which technical parameters to clarify and what an initial comparison experiment should establish to evaluate a remote, fiber-coupled optical measurement of water in a petroleum stream.

recommendations.rationale: Mid-IR fundamental absorption bands provide high chemical selectivity and sensitivity for water, supported by demonstrated precedent measuring water in petroleum with ATR probes. The ATR geometry limits optical path length to a few micrometers, accommodating opaque or absorbing hydrocarbon matrices.
recommendations.conditions: Applicable if the distance to the analyzer is compatible with mid-IR fiber attenuation and the stream permits direct optical crystal contact.

citations.quote: Application: measurement of water content in petroleum
ATR fiber probes (Fig.1) enable the analysis of liquids and solid elastic samples

recommendations.rationale: Near-infrared spectroscopy coupled via low-OH silica fibers allows remote analyzer placement over extended distances away from the process line. It serves as an alternative if the transmission distance precludes mid-IR fibers and the stream is sufficiently transparent.
recommendations.conditions: Requires the petroleum stream to be transparent or semi-transparent with water concentrations high enough for overtone band detection.

citations.quote: Robust 100-300m cables made with Silica fibers of low OH-content (<0.1ppm OH) enable remote industrial process-control
Transmission is the preferred method for transparent or semi-transparent liquids, such as skim milk, whey, or permeate.

measurement_concept.probe_and_geometry: An in-line ATR immersion probe with a zirconium oxide or diamond crystal tip for mid-IR, or an immersion transmission/transflection probe with a controlled optical gap (1-10 mm) for NIR.
measurement_concept.location: Directly mounted in the petroleum process line or a conditioned fast-loop bypass closer to the operation, sending light to the remote analyzer shelter.
measurement_concept.fiber_link: Polycrystalline (PIR) or chalcogenide (CIR) infrared fibers for mid-IR over short runs, or robust low-OH silica fibers for extended remote distances in NIR.

assessment.chemometrics_note: A quantitative multivariate calibration (such as PLS regression) will be required to resolve water absorption peaks from overlapping hydrocarbon matrix signals and baseline shifts, with models validated against independent reference samples.
assessment.realtime_tracking_note: Continuous optical spectra acquired by an in-line fiber immersion probe will allow near real-time trending of moisture content, alerting operators to process upsets much faster than off-line laboratory sampling.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the physical routing distance from the process line to the analyzer exceeds mid-IR fiber capabilities, or if the stream is transparent and demands long fiber lengths, the recommended choice would switch to option O2.
proposal.next_step: Obtain representative samples of the petroleum stream spanning normal and elevated water levels to perform initial benchtop mid-IR ATR and NIR feasibility trials against laboratory Karl Fischer reference data.

assessment.brief_answer: Mid-IR ATR spectroscopy should be evaluated first, supported by demonstrated precedent for measuring water in petroleum streams, with NIR transmission as an alternative if long fiber distances are required. Key open factors include the expected water concentration range, stream transparency, and the exact distance to the external analyzer. A laboratory feasibility comparison on representative petroleum samples against Karl Fischer titration is recommended to establish sensitivity and detection limits.

assessment.chemometrics_note: A quantitative multivariate calibration (such as PLS regression) will be required to resolve water absorption peaks from overlapping hydrocarbon matrix signals and baseline shifts, with models validated against independent reference samples.
assessment.realtime_tracking_note: Continuous optical spectra acquired by an in-line fiber immersion probe will allow near real-time trending of moisture content, alerting operators to process upsets much faster than off-line laboratory sampling.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the physical routing distance from the process line to the analyzer exceeds mid-IR fiber capabilities, or if the stream is transparent and demands long fiber lengths, the recommended choice would switch to option O2.
proposal.next_step: Obtain representative samples of the petroleum stream spanning normal and elevated water levels to perform initial benchtop mid-IR ATR and NIR feasibility trials against laboratory Karl Fischer reference data.

assessment.brief_answer: Mid-IR ATR spectroscopy should be evaluated first, supported by demonstrated precedent for measuring water in petroleum streams, with NIR transmission as an alternative if long fiber distances are required. Key open factors include the expected water concentration range, stream transparency, and the exact distance to the external analyzer. A laboratory feasibility comparison on representative petroleum samples against Karl Fischer titration is recommended to establish sensitivity and detection limits.

items.finding: Water OH bands in NIR and MIR spectra exhibit strong temperature sensitivity, requiring tempered sample holders during aqueous measurements.
items.how_it_applies: This highlights the importance of monitoring or compensating for process fluid temperature when tracking water bands in optical measurements.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited study addresses aqueous biopharmaceutical solutions rather than water traces within a petroleum stream, and it refers to sample holder tempering rather than in-line RTD or thermocouple compensation.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
